column2: Software Development using AI
UG

This course examines modern AI-native software development, focusing on how developers collaborate with coding agents. Designed for advanced undergraduate students, it covers defining intent, context engineering, structuring development workflows, and coordinating AI tools. Rather than serving as a general introduction to machine learning, a traditional programming course, or a theoretical study of large language models, it emphasizes practical, workflow-oriented software engineering. Students will learn to configure AI coding tools using Model Context Protocol servers, construct executable specifications from natural language requirements, and analyze iterative agentic debugging loops. They will also evaluate automated testing, deployment, and reliability metrics for agent-generated artifacts, culminating in the delivery of an end-to-end software application. The course is taught through three hours of lectures, one hour of tutorial, and two hours of practical labs per week over thirteen weeks, heavily incorporating hands-on development and a collaborative group project.

Course Code: Configure AI coding tools and agent skills within a given development environment, integrating Model Context Protocol servers to support developer workflows, such that all public integration checks pass and no configuration warnings are reported.
column2: Construct executable specifications from natural language requirements using spec-driven development tools, for a supplied functional specification document, covering every use case in the supplied requirements document.
column3: Analyze agent-assisted software development loops and iterative workflows, for a supplied project codebase of at most 5000 lines of code within 60 minutes, identifying at least three distinct failure causes with supporting log evidence.
column4: Evaluate automated testing, deployment, and reliability metrics for an agent-generated software artifact, identifying at least three distinct reliability vulnerabilities, with a proposed mitigation for each.
column5: Evaluate an end-to-end software application through collaborative agent workflows, such that the delivered system satisfies every acceptance criterion agreed at the first milestone and is demonstrated live with three scenario walkthroughs chosen by the evaluator.
